51577374.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 LasR assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - 4.15. Protein SP: The proteins were extracted from the overexpressed strains of E. coli BL21-LasR and E. coli BL21-PqsR and preserved in the laboratory, followed by a molecule-protein analysis using surface plasmon resonance (SPR) interaction. Betterware Inc. provided chemically modified label-free photo-cross-linker sensor chips for the experiment. A BioDot AD-1520 Array Printer was used to print samples and controls on the chip surface with a volume of 1.875 nL/dot, forming 5 nonadjacent repetitions of each sample on the same chip. The flow cell chambers were assembled onto the chip surface. SPR testing was conducted using a bScreen LB 991 Label-free Microarray System from BERTHOLD TECHNOLOGIES to monitor real-time protein interaction. During SPR testing, HBS-EP running buffer and running buffer (1 × PBS with 5 % DMSO) were used to prime the chip surface injecting LasR and PqsR proteins at various concentrations over 600 s at a flow rate of 0.5 μL/s in each associating stage followed by running buffer for dissociation stages lasting for 360 s at a flow rate of 0.5 μL/s. Surface regeneration was performed after each associating-dissociating cycle using a pulse of glycine-HCl (pH 2.5) at a rate of 20 μL/min for 30 s to remove any remaining bound material on the surface. Blank controls and background noise controls were tested individually during the testing process using DMSO solvents for chemical compounds and PBS (pH = 7.0) solvents for proteins, respectively.

(A) SPR interaction and affinity analysis of compound A9 and LasR; (B) SPR interaction and affinity analysis of solvent control DMSO and LasR; (C) SPR interaction and affinity analysis of compound A9 and PqsR; (D) SPR interaction and affinity analysis of solvent control DMSO and PqsR.
